epics.title: Podcast Media Hub
epics.jtbd: When a visitor wants to listen to the podcast, I want to browse episodes with detailed show notes and audio playback, so that I can consume the audio content directly.
requirements: R1: Sync episodes from podcast/YouTube archive with key insights, timestamps, and quotes.
R2: Organize content in Tier 2: The Stream / Episodes with unified media player.

slices.title: Podcast Episode Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the episode sync for this epic, I want a structured schema for episodes, timestamps, and quotes, so that media playback and metadata are deeply integrated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new podcast episode payload,
When the data layer processes it,
Then it is saved with a unified media player format, exact timestamps, and concept links.

slices.title: Episode Player UI Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the media hub UI for this epic, I want a unified media player layout, so that visitors can listen while reading timestamps and core theses.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an episode with timestamps,
When a visitor opens the Stream tier,
Then the unified media player loads, timestamp clicks seek the audio accurately, and the UI complies with WCAG 2.1 AA (keyboard operability, visible focus, labelled form controls, 4.5:1 text contrast).

slices.title: QA Media Hub Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want comprehensive tests covering playback and data sync, so that broken episodes are prevented.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a mocked episode payload,
When the test suite runs,
Then the sync pipeline, schema validation, and player rendering succeed across the test pyramid.

epics.title: Real Thought Stream and Insights Sync
epics.jtbd: When a visitor browses the fast stream, I want to see real-time insights synchronized from Telegram, so that I can consume quantized thoughts directly.
requirements: R1: Sync real-world insights from Telegram channel @efremov_mvp.
R2: Organize content in Tier 3: The Sparks / Quantized Thoughts.

slices.title: Thought Stream Data Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the Telegram sync for this epic, I want a structured schema for quantized thoughts, so that parsed insights are stored efficiently.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a Telegram payload,
When the webhook receives it,
Then it is mapped and persisted correctly in the Sparks schema.

slices.title: Telegram Webhook Integration API
slices.jtbd: When implementing Telegram sync for this epic, I want a secure webhook receiver, so that quantized thoughts are ingested immediately.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a webhook payload from Telegram,
When the API processes it,
Then the insight is authenticated and persisted in the Sparks tier format.

slices.title: The Sparks UI Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the Sparks UI for this epic, I want a fast-stream layout, so that visitors can quickly scroll through quantized thoughts.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a stream of synced insights,
When the visitor views Tier 3,
Then the insights render immediately with a clean editorial style and the UI complies with WCAG 2.1 AA (keyboard operability, visible focus, labelled form controls, 4.5:1 text contrast).

slices.title: QA Real Thought Stream Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want integration tests for the Telegram webhook and UI rendering, so that missing messages are caught.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a simulated Telegram payload,
When the integration test suite runs,
Then it verifies the payload is saved and correctly surfaced in the UI stream.

epics.title: Sovereign Canon and Ontology Architecture
epics.jtbd: When a visitor explores the site, I want to read the Evergreen manifestos and ontology across structured domains, so that I understand the core architectural philosophy.
requirements: R1: Organize content in Tier 1: The Canon (Evergreen manifestos, ontology, glossary).
R2: Organize across 4 practical domains: Autonomous Engineering, Agentic Economy (A2A), Pragmatic Business Strategy, Philosophy of Mind.
R3: Replace all placeholder/mock content with genuine intellectual artifacts.

slices.title: Canon Content Schema and Taxonomy
slices.jtbd: When implementing the Canon structure for this epic, I want a robust schema supporting 4 domains and deep linking, so that manifestos can cross-reference properly.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a glossary term or manifesto,
When it is stored in the database,
Then it is strongly typed to one of the 4 domains and supports relational links.

slices.title: Canon Reader UI Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the Canon UI for this epic, I want a premium editorial reading experience, so that deep philosophical texts are comfortable to consume.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a long-form manifesto in a domain,
When a visitor loads the Canon tier,
Then it displays with semantic HTML5, cross-link navigation, and the UI complies with WCAG 2.1 AA (keyboard operability, visible focus, labelled form controls, 4.5:1 text contrast).

slices.title: QA Sovereign Canon Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify content domains and real artifact ingestion, so that the canon is accurate and placeholder-free.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the initial genuine artifacts,
When the E2E test asserts content,
Then it ensures no placeholder text exists and all 4 domains are correctly populated.

epics.title: Distribution and SEO
epics.jtbd: When external platforms or RSS readers index the site, I want them to receive structured metadata and feeds, so that the content is correctly distributed and previewed.
requirements: R1: Provide /.well-known/llms.txt and /.well-known/ai-agent.json providing clean markdown index of all concepts.
R2: Semantic SEO & Open Graph meta tags optimized for LLM web crawlers.
R3: Clean high-density text representations without heavy DOM/JS blocking for machine readers.

slices.title: LLM Well-Known Manifest API
slices.jtbd: When implementing LLM distribution for this epic, I want dynamic /.well-known endpoints, so that bots get real-time markdown indexes.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a request to /.well-known/llms.txt or ai-agent.json,
When an external agent crawls it,
Then a valid, high-density plain text or JSON index of the Canon is returned.

slices.title: Semantic SEO Meta Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing SEO for this epic, I want to inject Open Graph and semantic tags, so that PerplexityBot and GPTBot index the site properly.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a Canon or Stream page,
When a crawler parses the head,
Then Open Graph tags and semantic metadata are present and valid, ensuring the output also strictly complies with WCAG 2.1 AA where applicable.

slices.title: QA SEO and Machine Readability Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to validate the output formats of well-known endpoints and meta tags, so that crawlers are never blocked.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the live endpoints,
When the test suite parses them,
Then it validates the exact markdown format, JSON structure, and DOM presence of SEO tags.

epics.title: Confidential Client Intake
epics.jtbd: When a prospective client submits an idea, I want a secure, black-box intake flow, so that commercial confidentiality is guaranteed and internal factory mechanics are hidden.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Zero data leaks of factory mechanics
requirements: R1: Strict Black Box invariant: Zero internal factory mechanics exposed to visitors.
R2: Clean client intake: Input idea/wishlist -> output turnkey result.
R3: Commercial confidentiality and NDA guaranteed.

slices.title: Client Intake Data Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the intake schema for this epic, I want a secure data model, so that confidential inputs are persisted properly.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a validated client wishlist payload,
When saving to the data layer,
Then the schema mandates encrypted fields at rest.

slices.title: Secure Client Intake API
slices.jtbd: When implementing the intake API for this epic, I want a secure endpoint for wishlists, so that NDA-bound data is safely ingested.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a submitted wishlist,
When the backend receives it,
Then it is encrypted at rest and acknowledged without exposing internal systemic logs.

slices.title: Black-Box Intake UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing the intake UI for this epic, I want a clean, NDA-focused form, so that the client experience remains premium and obfuscates factory mechanics.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the intake page,
When a user submits an idea,
Then they receive confirmation, no internal references leak, and the UI complies with WCAG 2.1 AA (keyboard operability, visible focus, labelled form controls, 4.5:1 text contrast).

slices.title: QA Confidentiality and Black Box Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want E2E tests validating that no internal keywords leak, so that the NDA invariant holds.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a full submission flow,
When the E2E suite inspects the DOM and network,
Then it asserts the absence of internal factory terms and verifies secure storage.

epics.title: Platform Telemetry and Measurement
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want to measure visitor engagement with my content and external links, so that I know if the site successfully drives interest in my work.
requirements: R1: Track visitor engagement with the three-tier content structure (Canon, Stream, Sparks) and client intake flow.
R2: Implement Goal-Question-Metric: Goal = drive agentic economy engagement; Questions = Do visitors read the Canon? Do they submit intake forms? Metrics = Canon dwell time, form conversion rate.

slices.title: GQM Telemetry Instrumentation
slices.jtbd: When implementing telemetry for this epic, I want to track Canon dwell time and form conversions, so that GQM questions are accurately answered.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a user reading the Canon or submitting an intake,
When the action completes,
Then an anonymized telemetry event is sent to the backend, and any UI elements introduced comply with WCAG 2.1 AA.

slices.title: QA Telemetry Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify event firing, so that measurement accuracy is guaranteed.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given simulated user engagement,
When the tests monitor the network,
Then the correct GQM metrics are fired exactly once per action.

epics.title: Initial Content and Acceptance
epics.jtbd: When receiving the delivered system, I want to see it populated with realistic content, so that I can verify all paths and features work end-to-end.
requirements: R1: Populate the system with a complete set of genuine intellectual artifacts, a podcast episode, and sample telegram sparks.
R2: Ensure all tiers (Canon, Stream, Sparks) have enough realistic content to demonstrate the full end-to-end user path.

slices.title: Acceptance Seed Data Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the seed data for this epic, I want a robust database seeder, so that the deployed instance is immediately demonstrable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a fresh deployment,
When the system boots,
Then the database is populated with genuine manifestos, an episode, and sample sparks.

slices.title: QA Acceptance Walkthrough Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want an E2E test verifying content presence, so that the system is proven to hold the required assets.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a seeded database,
When the E2E test navigates all three tiers,
Then it asserts the visibility of specific real-world insights and podcast titles.

epics.title: Privacy Consent Management
epics.jtbd: When a visitor arrives on the site, I want to be asked for consent before any non-essential trackers load, so that my privacy preferences are respected and the site complies with ePrivacy regulations.
requirements: R1: Opt-in consent captured before any non-essential cookie or tracker loads; refusing must be as easy as accepting.
R2: Use an established consent platform rather than a hand-rolled banner.

slices.title: Consent Platform Integration
slices.jtbd: When implementing consent for this epic, I want to integrate a third-party consent banner, so that GDPR and ePrivacy duties are met.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new visitor session,
When the site loads,
Then an established consent platform banner is presented, blocks telemetry until approved, and the banner UI complies with WCAG 2.1 AA (keyboard operability, visible focus, labelled form controls, 4.5:1 text contrast).

slices.title: QA Privacy Consent Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify that no trackers leak before consent, so that the regulatory floor is respected.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a fresh visitor,
When the site is accessed without clicking the banner,
Then no tracking cookies or scripts execute in the browser context.

epics.title: Data Protection and Recovery
epics.jtbd: When the database experiences a failure, I want to be able to restore the system state from a backup, so that I do not lose my published content.
requirements: R1: Regular backups of the core Postgres database containing the Canon, Stream, and Intake data.
R2: A tested and verified restore process, not merely configured.

slices.title: Automated Backup Configuration
slices.jtbd: When implementing backups for this epic, I want scheduled pg_dump scripts, so that data loss risk is mitigated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the production database,
When the cron schedule triggers,
Then a complete SQL dump is generated and stored securely offsite.

slices.title: QA Data Restoration Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to perform a real restore in a test environment, so that the backup is proven valid.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a generated backup file,
When the restoration script is executed on a clean container,
Then the database fully recovers and passes all content integrity checks.

epics.title: Data Subject Rights and GDPR Compliance
epics.jtbd: When a user whose personal data was submitted by an AI agent requests access or deletion, I want to be able to export or erase their data within the statutory deadline, so that the system complies with privacy regulations.
requirements: R1: Export of a data subject's own data (e.g. from the client intake form) on request.
R2: Erasure of a data subject's own data on request within the statutory deadline.

slices.title: GDPR Data Rights API
slices.jtbd: When implementing GDPR tooling for this epic, I want an admin endpoint to export or delete intake records, so that compliance requests are fulfilled quickly.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an administrator processing a request,
When the endpoint is invoked with an email address,
Then the associated intake data is either securely exported as JSON or permanently deleted.

slices.title: QA GDPR Compliance Coverage
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify complete data erasure, so that no residual personal data remains.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an intake record in the database,
When the deletion API is called,
Then subsequent queries confirm the record is completely removed from all tables.
